title: The committed tokenized WordPress theme stylesheets are what the tokenizer makes of them today: wp-ja-vega.css (1.1.14) keeps its accordion toggle's literal pair, so a REG-PR-1087 run leaves no tracked diff
steps: S1: From packages/design/tracy-ds-slot run: node --test --test-reporter=tap test/tokenize.test.mjs
S2: Record the exit code, '# fail' and the result of the test 'every tokenized WordPress theme stylesheet in the tree is what the tokenizer makes of it today'.
expect: 'every tokenized WordPress theme stylesheet in the tree is what the tokenizer makes of it today' is ok: for every templates/wordpress-*.json whose theme's overlay stylesheet reads --ds-c-*, tokenizing that stylesheet again with the contract's palette changes no line, wp-ja-vega among at least six themes checked — so .jv-accordion__button::after paints color: #050505 on its literal #f0f1f2 disc (on 977cbb3e6 the test names wp-ja-vega.css as stale: that line read var(--ds-c-fg-2, #050505)).

selectors.rule: src/tokenize.mjs literalFill (a rule that keeps its fill literal keeps its text literal)

evidence: 10/10/2026: re-tokenizing the committed wp-ja-vega.css (1.1.13, released to TracyHQ/claude-cowork on 09/10 with the same bytes) changed line 2521 'color: var(--ds-c-fg-2, #050505)' to 'color: #050505' in the overlay and the built src copy; every REG-PR-1087 S4 run left that diff in the tree.
fence: the tokenized stylesheets committed for the WordPress themes; not the Joomla releases (their tokenized sheets live in the release archives)

tests: every tokenized WordPress theme stylesheet in the tree is what the tokenizer makes of it today
